type rank =
  | Ace
  | King
  | Queen
  | Jack
  | Num of int

type suit = Diamonds | Spades | Hearts | Clubs
type card = suit * rank

type winner = Lead | Follow

(* You can use this if you'd ike to do some debugging. *)
let name_of_card (suit, rank : card) : string = 
  let suit_name = match suit with
    | Hearts -> "hearts"
    | Spades -> "spades"
    | Clubs  -> "clubs"
    | Diamonds -> "diamonds" 
  in
  let rank_name = match rank with
    | Ace -> "ace"
    | Jack -> "jack"
    | Queen -> "queen"
    | King -> "king"
    | Num n -> string_of_int n
  in
  rank_name ^ " of " ^ suit_name

descr:
Schnapsen

This problem is a more advanced exercise with an ADT and pattern matching.

In this problem, we'll look at some function related to playing a card game called Schnapsen (but don't worry - we won't be playing the whole game).

You are given the definitions of the suit, rank, card, and hand types from lecture. (If we haven't gotten to that example yet, you can wait or read the given code yourself.) You're also given the enumeration type type winner = Lead | Follow.

You can see the definitions in the pane above the editor to the left. To reiterate, this pane is called the prelude. You can use anything defined there, but you can't edit it. You must not copy the prelude into your own code - this would make your code shadow the prelude, and then your code will no longer be compatible with the grader.

The game

Schapsen is what's called a "trick-taking" game. Each player plays one card. Then, one of those two cards wins, and whoever played it takes both cards. That player scores the point value of those cards and adds it to their total; the goal of the game is to reach 66 points. Each instance of playing two cards and someone taking them is called a "trick," the first card played to each trick is called the "lead," and the second card "follows the lead."

Schnapsen is played with a "William Tell deck" of cards, consisting of the aces, tens, and face card. The point values are as follows:

  • Jack, 2
  • Queen, 3
  • King, 4
  • Ten, 10
  • Ace, 11

In every hand of Schnapsen, there is a "trump suit." Cards of the trump suit always beat cards not of the trump suit. This may be familiar from other card games - the idea is the same!

Altogether, the winner of a trick is as follows:

  • If exactly one card belongs to the trump suit, that card wins.
  • Otherwise, if both cards belong to the same suit, the one worth more points wins.
  • Otherwise, the lead card wins.

The problem

First, we need a way to get the point value of a card. Complete the implementation of point_value.

Then, determine who wins a trick; given a trump suit, a lead card, and a follow card, return either Lead or Follow to indicate which card wins the trick.

Aside

Schnapsen is the most interesting two-player card game that I (TA Max) know. It has a somewhat rich history of AI development as well, and only recently have the best AIs become better than the best humans. Bring a pack of cards and find me sometime and I'd be happy to teach anyone how to play.
